    How the Minesweeper Probability Calculator Works

    This calculator treats the entered rectangle as a complete, closed board: clues have no unknown neighbors outside it and flags are assumed correct. It counts all valid local arrangements equally. It does not use a whole-board mine total or outside clues, so percentages are local-model estimates, not exact odds for your full game. Only transfer deductions if these assumptions match your position.

    1. Certain Safe Reveals (0% Mine)

    If every valid mine arrangement leaves a specific covered square empty, that square is 100% safe (0% mine). It is highlighted in green. You can reveal it immediately without risk.

    2. Proven Mines (100% Mine)

    If every valid mine arrangement requires a specific square to be mined, that square is 100% mined. It is highlighted in red. You can flag it with complete certainty.

    3. Local 50/50 and Ambiguous Positions

    A 50% result means half of the equally weighted local arrangements contain a mine there. Outside clues and the remaining mine total may change the odds or resolve the position. This alone does not prove an unavoidable whole-board 50/50.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    How do I solve from a screenshot?

    Simply take a screenshot of your Minesweeper board (e.g. Win+Shift+S on Windows or Cmd+Shift+4 on Mac), return to this page, and press Ctrl+V (or Cmd+V). The computer vision algorithm automatically aligns the grid and identifies numbers.

    How does this solver calculate mine probabilities?

    The solver enumerates arrangements satisfying the entered clues, treating the rectangle as closed and flags as correct. Percentages weight these local arrangements equally; outside clues and the global mine total are not included.

    What is the difference between this solver and No Guess mode?

    This calculator analyzes any ambiguous position you input. In contrast, No Guess Minesweeper verifies a deduction-only path from your first click before accepting a board. If verification fails within the generation limit, it asks you to start a new game.

    When should you guess in a 50/50 position?

    Check all other clues and the remaining mine total first. A local 50% estimate does not establish a forced guess or the best whole-board move.
